title: Windowed burst debiting and prorated SLA compensation model
creator: Aditi Rao
description:
Problem: Dedicated pools support reserved throughput and short-lived burst consumption. Current accounting charges bursts to instant leaky-bucket counters which leads to unfair tenant debiting across overlapping reserved windows, mismatched SLA credit calculations in partial-pool degradations, and noisy retroactive reconciliations. Operators and customers report confusing invoices where a tenant's short burst appears to consume a disproportionate portion of a reservation and where SLA credits appear either over- or under-apportioned after a degraded interval.

Goal: Implement a windowed, prorated debit model that (1) allocates burst consumption across the reservation timeline proportionally, (2) computes SLA compensation using a time-weighted expected throughput shadow-meter, and (3) produces deterministic per-tenant ledger entries that are easy to audit and reconcile. The model must be compatible with current quota enforcement (leaky buckets and token-buckets), support retroactive correction with idempotent reconciliation, and keep cost/latency overhead within current accounting budgets.

High-level approach:
- Introduce a time-windowed burst debit aggregation that buffers short bursts (< 5s) and attributes consumption across windows aligned to the reservation granularity (default 1 minute, configurable per-pool).
- Maintain a lightweight shadow-meter that records expected reserved-availability per-tenant for each window; use this to compute prorated SLA credits for partial pool degradation.
- Emit deterministic ledger events for each window with unique window IDs; reconciliation runs can re-emit the same events idempotently to correct prior offsets.
- Ensure enforcement and charging paths remain read-path fast: the runtime enforces soft limits by leaky buckets but triggers a non-blocking accounting write to the window aggregator.
- Provide observability: dashboards for per-window attribution, an explainable ledger API for customer invoices, and a reconciliation report for finance.

Risks and trade-offs: buffering bursts adds a small latency to accounting writes (not request latency). Complexity in window alignment across cross-region pools needs careful time-sync and fallback. Retroactive corrections must avoid double-crediting customers; we will use monotonically increasing window offsets and idempotency keys for ledger writes.
acceptance_criteria: Windowed debit aggregator implemented: burst consumption (<= 5s) is aggregated into 1-minute windows by default and tagged with a deterministic window ID.
Per-window ledger entries are emitted for all tenants and reconcile deterministically; re-running reconciliation for the same window is idempotent.
SLA credit calculator uses time-weighted shadow-meter to compute prorated credit for partial pool degradations; credits match expected math in spec and unit tests.
No customer-facing request latency increase; accounting write added asynchronously and does not block inference responses.
New telemetry dashboards show per-window reserved vs actual consumption, top offenders, and reconciliation diff; finance can export invoice-ready per-tenant ledgers.
Migration plan executed: historical windows older than 30 days can be compacted and reconciled; reconciliation on rollout yields zero net-customer-change for test pools.
End-to-end integration tests (unit + integration in staging) validate negative balance guards and correct credit amortization for multi-tenant pools.
tasks: Design: finalize math for prorated allocation and draft spec with examples (Aditi)
Runtime: add non-blocking accounting hook and window ID generation (Marcus)
Aggregator service: implement in Go, support window buffering and per-tenant aggregation, expose idempotent write API (Engops)
Ledger: extend ledger schema to include window_id and source_hint; implement idempotency keys and compact/rollup path (Billing)
SLA calculator: implement shadow-meter logic and unit tests for partial degradation scenarios (SRE)
APIs: expose explainable per-window ledger endpoint and reconcile-report export (Platform API)
Dashboards: build Grafana panels and finance export CSV template (Observability)
Migration: implement backfill/reconciliation job and run on staging; validate no-regressions on test customers (DataEng)
Docs + customer comms: update billing docs and draft support FAQ for expected invoice changes (Docs & CS)
End-to-end tests: create synthetic load tests for overlapping bursts and validate account balances and SLA crediting (QA)
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sync completed; agreed on default window size 1 minute and burst threshold 5s. Aditi posted initial spec in Confluence.
2026-03-05: Prototype aggregator written; proof-of-concept shows reduced invoice churn in simulated multi-tenant bursts. Found edge-case with region clock skew > 200ms.
2026-03-09: Design review feedback: Finance requested export column for pre- and post-credit balances; added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-12: Runtime hook implemented as async write; initial benchmark shows accounting write adds 0.2ms p95 overhead to request processing (acceptable).
2026-03-14: Aggregator service tests cover idempotency and compact path. Starting staging rollout for two small dedicated pools next week.
comments: Sofia Martinez (Product): This should make invoices easier to explain to customers who run spiky workloads — please include illustrative invoice examples in docs.
Ezra Cohen (Billing): Ensure ledger rollup retains sufficient detail for chargebacks; Finance wants both per-window and per-day rollups.
Priya Nair (SRE): Clock skew mitigation: if cross-region pool clocks differ, aggregator will fall back to logical window alignment using pool leader. We'll validate in chaos test.
Design review (2026-03-09): agreed to expose a knob for window size per-pool for customers that bought minute-level reservations.
